 ABC News News Home Police find teenager alive six days after he disappeared in Gippsland bush Share Share article Police find teenager alive six days after he disappeared in Gippsland bush
 By Daniel Miles , Lily Kristanto and Jack Colantuono ABC Gippsland
 Topic: Missing Person
 Posted Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 12:04pm Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 12:04pm Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 12:04pm , updated Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 9:30pm Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 9:30pm Thu 12 Nov 2026 at 9:30pm Loading... In short:
 A police helicopter crew has found and winched to safety a teenager who had disappeared in bushland in Victoria's east six days ago.
 The 17-year-old disappeared on Friday while on a camping trip with his friend.
 The boy was reunited with his mother before being taken to hospital for monitoring.
 abc.net.au/news/missing-teenager-william-found-gippsland-bush/107372518 Link copied Share Share article A teenager survived six days in dense bushland in Victoria's east by using two towels as blankets to combat freezing nights and rationing a family sized bag of chicken chips.
 William, 17, is recovering in hospital after a police helicopter found him sleeping in a dry riverbed.
 The teenager, whose surname has not been released, disappeared on Friday while camping with a friend at Walhalla East, about 180 kilometres east of Melbourne.
 His disappearance sparked an intense six-day search i nvolving hundreds of people, including police divers, the dog squad and helicopters.
 His mother, Elizabeth Barkley, told A Current Affair (ACA) that she was shocked how well her son was after his ordeal.
 "He's in a talkative spirit — he's happy, he's hungry," she said late on Thursday.
 Ms Barkley said William had wanted McDonald's, so she delivered his order to him: one quarter pounder, six nuggets, a cheeseburger and large fries.
 "Except for a bit of sunburn and scratches … his leg's a bit sore from the scratches, he's in fighting spirit and I just can't believe how well he handled being out there for so long," she told ACA.
 Elizabeth Barkley breaks down in tears while discussing her son's disappearance. ( ABC News ) 
 William, who was on his first independent camping trip, was found sleeping on a rock in a dry riverbed by a helicopter crew who spotted his fishing tackle box about 2 kilometres east of Stoney Creek this morning.
 He was shirtless and sunburned, with a pillow, lunch box and small table nearby.
 William smiled, waved, then pumped his fist when he awoke to the sound of the police helicopter circling overhead.
 His mother told ACA that being reunited with her son after his rescue felt like an "out-of-body experience".
 "I was just so happy, and then when he said 'I love you Mum', that just melted my heart."
 Police said William had spent days walking through extremely rugged and rocky terrain before he fell down a steep riverbed embankment two days ago.
 He spent the past two days sleeping and waiting to be found.
 William was last seen on Friday, about 4pm. ( Supplied: Victoria Police ) 
 His mum told ACA her son had missed a turn-off back to his camp, so curled up under some bushes and fell asleep.
 "He said he got up the next day and started walking again, trying to find the camp site, and he just missed his footing and down he went."
 Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said the teen woke up to the sound of the helicopter and gave rescuers a wave before being winched to safety.
 "The search area today was something we couldn't do on foot, it was way too steep and beyond the capabilities of any human, to be honest."
 Police said William was exhausted and unable to walk, with cuts on his legs. He also had severe sunburn to his upper body and face.
 Police found the teenager six days after he disappeared while camping near Cowwarr. ( ABC News: Lily Kristanto ) 
 "Other than that, he's talking to us, he's happy, he's smiling, he's giving us an account of what's happening and he's hugging his mother and having a doughnut and water," Acting Inspector Benbow said.
 William's mother earlier fought back tears as she spoke to the media shortly after they had been reunited in Cowwarr.
 "He's never leaving the house again. He's grounded for life," she said. "He's not going anywhere ever again. I'm just over the moon."
 William has been taken to Latrobe Regional Hospital with his mother for monitoring.
 The hospital's CEO, Don McRae, said it was "extraordinary to see him so well".
 "He's obviously a fit young man and I think that's really held him in good stead."
 All going well, William could be discharged as early as tomorrow.
 Mother never gave up hope
 A huge number of people joined the search for the 17-year-old over six days, with more than 80 volunteers scouring the bush each day.
 His mother never gave up on him being found, despite the fact he had little bush experience.
 Loading... "I knew in my heart he was still alive," Ms Barkley said.
 "I could feel it. I knew he wasn't gone. Thank God he's such [a] fit person."
 The pair were reunited this morning when Ms Barkley happened to be at the police staging ground in Cowwarr.
 She ran to the police helicopter with open arms, embracing her son before telling him: "You scared the shit out of me."
 William went missing while on a camping trip at Walhalla East on Friday, November 6. ( Supplied: Victoria Police ) 
 William could be seen smiling and laughing with police while sitting with his legs outside the helicopter's side door.
 Authorities said it would not have been possible to find William without the police helicopter.
 "I've been praying for this all week. To find him while I was out here, it was such a perfect … you couldn't write the script any better ," his mother said.
 William could be seen smiling and scratching his head after his six-day ordeal came to an end. ( ABC News ) 
 Dreams of football fame
 Speaking on the boundary line of the Cowwarr Recreation Reserve, Ms Barkley revealed her son had dreams of becoming a famous AFL footballer.
 "[He wanted] to be famous that way, not famous like this," she said, smiling.
 "But I don't care. He's mine now.
 " And he's definitely never ever going camping ever [again] unless it's in a cabin and it's with me, and I'll have one of those rope things that you tie to kids so they don't wander off. " William was located alive and assessed by paramedics. ( ABC News: Lily Kristanto ) 
 Ms Barkley thanked the volunteers who spent countless hours searching for her son.
 SES incident controller Tohi Kuru was with police and Ms Barkley when news broke William had been found.
 "There was just this air that came in, no-one was saying anything … we knew something was coming," he said.
 "A few minutes later we had confirmation [he had been found] … it was an awe-inspiring moment to watch that mother reunite with William."
 'Best thing about the job'
 Victoria Police Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said it was an amazing feeling when William was found.
 He said William "had no idea police were even looking for him".
 "In my opinion, I think he could have survived more days; he was very fit and healthy," he said.
 Acting Inspector Jason Benbow says finding William after six days of searching is one of the highlights of his career. ( ABC News: Lily Kristanto ) 
 "It's just amazing how he's survived this long, through cold nights, hot days.
 "There's a few emotional police in there … this is the best thing about the job; to have this sort of result at the end.
 "It doesn't happen all the time."
 His mother said she planned to give her son so many hugs that police may have to become involved again.
 "He'll have to get a restraining order out on me, because I'm not going to let him go," she jokingly told ACA.
 Victoria Police could be seen celebrating William's safe return today. ( ABC News: Lily Kristanto )
